question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Early English trading factories in India and their location]
options: Surat – Gujarat, first major English factory (1608/1613)
Masulipatnam – Andhra (Coromandel Coast), first English factory in South India
Fort St. George (Madras) – founded 1639, Coromandel Coast
wrong_fact: Fort William (Calcutta/Kolkata) was established in 1696, NOT 1600. The English East India Company itself was founded in 1600, but Fort William was built nearly a century later.
explanation: The English East India Company received its charter in 1600 but Fort William in Calcutta was constructed in 1696 (formally completed 1700) by Job Charnock's successors. Surat was indeed the first major factory (factory rights granted 1613 after the Battle of Swally), Masulipatnam was established in the 1610s, and Fort St. George was founded in 1639.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [English naval engagements against Portuguese and their location]
options: Battle of Swally (1612) – Near Surat, Arabian Sea
Capture of Hormuz (1622) – Strait of Hormuz, Persian Gulf entrance
Battle of Diu (1612) – Gulf of Khambhat (Cambay), English vs Portuguese
English pressure on Mughal ports – Surat region, leading to Mughal preference for English
wrong_fact: There was no significant 'Battle of Diu (1612)' between English and Portuguese in the Gulf of Khambhat. The famous Battle of Diu was in 1509 between the Portuguese and a combined Muslim fleet. The key English-Portuguese naval battle was at Swally (1612).
explanation: The Battle of Swally (1612) near Surat was the defining English naval victory over the Portuguese, impressing the Mughal Emperor. In 1622, English forces allied with Persia to capture Hormuz from Portugal. There is no historically significant 'Battle of Diu (1612)' between English and Portuguese — the Battle of Diu (1509) was a Portuguese victory over Egyptian, Ottoman, and Indian Muslim fleets.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [English expansion displacing Portuguese influence and the region/port]
options: Bombay – Given to England as part of Catherine of Braganza's dowry, 1661
Madras (Fort St. George) – Established 1639, replaced Portuguese influence in Coromandel
Calcutta – Established late 17th century, bypassing Portuguese Bengal trading posts
Goa – Captured by English from Portuguese in the late 17th century
wrong_fact: Goa was NEVER captured by the English. It remained a Portuguese territory until 1961 when India annexed it. The English received Bombay (not Goa) as part of Catherine of Braganza's marriage dowry.
explanation: Goa remained under Portuguese control for the longest time among all Portuguese colonies in India, being liberated only by India's Operation Vijay in December 1961. Bombay was indeed ceded to the English Crown in 1661 as part of the marriage settlement between Charles II and Catherine of Braganza and then leased to the EIC in 1668. Fort St. George (Madras) was established in 1639 and Calcutta rose to prominence in the late 17th century.
